issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` is a coarse pre-filter; document why this is sound.
issues.detail: The fast path bails when the value has no digit-followed-by-`s`-or-`ms`. That's the right shape for a hot path, but it also matches things like `1s` inside strings/urls and `5something` won't match — fine, because the real parser runs after. A one-line comment naming this as a cheap pre-filter for the valueParser would save the next maintainer five minutes. GOOD-TASTE otherwise.

issues.description: No test demonstrating the perf win or guarding the early-return.
issues.detail: The patch is a behavior-preserving optimization, so existing tests should still pass — fine. But there's no regression test that the early-return doesn't skip a real violation (e.g. weird whitespace, case, vendor prefix on the value side). A single test with a value the regex accidentally rejects would lock this in. Not blocking.

review.summary: Small, scoped, readable patch that does exactly one thing: skip the expensive valueParser path when the declaration value clearly contains no time token. The diff matches the surrounding style, the early-return is placed before the now-deferred `vendor.unprefixed`/`toLowerCase` work, and the changeset is present. Verdict: ACCEPT with trivial fixup — add a one-line comment on `HAS_TIME` explaining it's a cheap pre-filter, and ideally a test pinning the early-return behavior. Talk is cheap; this is just code that makes the rule faster. Land it.
